items.title: Inkling 2 Mini hits 65 tok/s on an M5 Ultra Mac Studio using the 17 GB 4-bit build in oMLX with its built-in draft model
items.summary: A builder reports 65 tokens per second decoding Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini on a Mac Studio, using the publicly downloadable 17 GB 4-bit build in oMLX with the model's built-in draft model enabled. It shows the new model runs fast on a single high-end Mac.

doubt.pushback: Single self-reported run with a screenshot; not reproduced by Magpie.

items.title: Two linked DGX Sparks process long prompts 26-28% faster when NCCL_IB_HCA lists both network devices of the cable
items.summary: Each Spark port appears as two network devices and a single one reaches about 112 of 200 Gb/s. Listing both in NCCL_IB_HCA speeds long-prompt processing by 26-28% in a two-Spark setup, with generation speed unchanged.

doubt.pushback: Self-reported measurement with no linked recipe or logs.

items.title: TensorFold tuning reaches 3,400 tok/s prefill and 80 tok/s decode on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on an M5 Ultra 512 GB Mac
items.summary: A TensorFold user reports prefill rising from 1,300 to 3,400 tokens per second and decode from 56 to 80 on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash running on a top-spec Mac, after some unspecified tuning. The post links the project page for details.

doubt.pushback: Numbers come from the author's own run and the tuning is not described in the post; the linked page was not read.

items.title: Analysis of Inkling 2 Mini weights: the looped design saves storage but reads about 5.5 GB per token, capping one Spark stream near 49 tok/s without speculative decoding
items.summary: Working from the official blog, config and weight file headers, the author shows the 26.4B MoE stores 24 layers but computes 48, so each token reads about 70% more bytes. On a 273 GB/s DGX Spark that bounds single-stream decode near 49 tok/s, and the bundled MTP head likely explains reports of 75.

doubt.pushback: Derived from tensor sizes, not a benchmark run; the MTP explanation is the author's guess.

items.title: Hugging Face reports early RL results training Qwen3.8-27B with thinking mode on harness adapters, with a Terminal-Bench 2.1 gain by step 70
items.summary: A Hugging Face post and blog describe adapting agent harnesses at scale and starting RL training of Qwen3.8-27B with thinking mode. The think harness adapter is reported much better at step 70 on 68 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks.

doubt.pushback: Early training signals only; the blog was not read for full numbers.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.329 adds a /tasks view to stop scheduled /loop jobs, wakeups and goals in a session
items.summary: Interval loops started with /loop could not be stopped with Esc or Ctrl+C and the docs only say to ask Claude to cancel them. From 2.1.329, /tasks lists the session's scheduled tasks, next loop wakeups and current goal so they can be managed there.

doubt.pushback: Second-hand description in Chinese of the changelog; changelog entry not read line by line.

items.title: Omarchy 4.5 shows a Process crashed alert and can hand the crash details to a coding agent to diagnose
items.summary: Omarchy 4.5 watches for app crashes and pops an alert; clicking Open starts the user's coding agent with the crash details prefilled so it can work out the cause.

doubt.pushback: Vendor demo video only; no changelog link read.
